chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who says 'Upon me is a vow' and he did not specify anything. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid (it amounts to nothing).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is not anything / It is invalid: a technical legal phrase signifying that the act has no legal force or effect
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow (nadhr): a voluntary religious commitment in which a person binds themselves to perform or abstain from an act for God's sake, conditional on a divine blessing or as an unconditional act of piety

ai.seo_question: Is a vow valid in Islam if no specific action or object is mentioned?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that a vow (nadhr) which lacks a specific object or action is legally void and carries no obligation. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, the validity of a vow requires precise specification of what is being committed; a vague declaration of 'I have a vow upon me' without naming the intended act or object cannot be legally binding. The original audience — jurists and practitioners in early Shia legal circles — would have understood this as establishing a foundational principle of the law of vows.
